questions.text: Study Source A. How useful is this source as evidence of Hitler's foreign policy ambitions? Explain your answer.
Study Source B. Why do you think Rothermere wrote this letter? Explain your answer.
Study Sources C and D. How far does Source D prove that Source C was wrong? Explain your answer.
Study Source E. Do you think the cartoonist would have agreed with Chamberlain's policy of appeasement? Explain your answer.

questions.command: How far do these sources support
questions.text: Study all the sources. 'Chamberlain was right to follow a policy of appeasement.' How far do these sources support this view? Use the sources and your knowledge to explain your answer.
'The main reason for the Dutch colonisation of Indonesia from the 1870s was to obtain raw materials.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.
'The main reason for the French colonisation of Vietnam from the 1870s was to obtain raw materials.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.
'Germans hated the Treaty of Versailles because it blamed them for starting World War I.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.
'US policy towards Japan in the 1930s was responsible for the outbreak of World War II in the Asia-Pacific.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.

content_units.name: Overview of Southeast Asia before 1870
content_units.description: A non-examinable introduction to the geography, peoples, political systems, and European interest in Southeast Asia prior to 1870.
content_units.evidence: Island and mainland Southeast Asia: Geography, people, political systems and the role of external influence

content_units.name: British Malaya, 1870s–1920s
content_units.description: Examines the extension of British control in Malaya, the transformation of its political, economic and social landscape, and local responses to colonial rule.
content_units.evidence: Extension of British control in Malaya… Shift in British policy towards Malaya in 1870s

content_units.name: Dutch Indonesia, 1870s–1920s
content_units.description: Covers the extension of Dutch control from Java to the Outer Islands, the transformation of Indonesia under Dutch rule, and local responses.
content_units.evidence: Extension of Dutch control in Indonesia from Java to the Outer Islands

content_units.name: French Vietnam, 1870s–1920s
content_units.description: Examines the extension of French control over Vietnam, the transformation of Vietnamese society and economy, and local responses to French rule.
content_units.evidence: Extension of French control in Vietnam to Annam and Tonkin

content_units.name: Paris Peace Conference and Post-WWI Europe
content_units.description: Studies the aims and terms of the Paris Peace Conference, the Treaty of Versailles, the redrawing of national boundaries, and attempts at collective security in the 1920s.
content_units.evidence: Aims and terms of the Paris Peace Conference and its immediate impact on Europe

content_units.name: Case Study of Nazi Germany
content_units.description: Examines the circumstances leading to the rise of Hitler and the Nazi Party, the consolidation of Nazi rule, and its political, economic and social policies.
content_units.evidence: Circumstances leading to the rise and establishment of authoritarian rule in Germany

content_units.name: Case Study of Militarist Japan, 1920s–1930s
content_units.description: Covers the rise of ultranationalist militarism in Japan, the weaknesses of democratic government, and the consolidation of military power and its policies.
content_units.evidence: Circumstances leading to the rise and establishment of authoritarian regime in Japan

content_units.name: Key Developments Leading to WWII in Europe
content_units.description: Examines the ineffectiveness of the League of Nations, Germany's aggressive foreign policy, and the policy of appeasement that led to the outbreak of World War II in Europe.
content_units.evidence: Key developments leading to the outbreak of World War II in Europe

content_units.name: Key Developments Leading to WWII in the Asia-Pacific
content_units.description: Covers Japan's expansionist foreign policy, worsening US-Japan relations, and the developments that led to the outbreak of World War II in the Asia-Pacific.
content_units.evidence: Key developments leading to the outbreak of World War II in the Asia-Pacific

content_units.name: Reasons for the End of World War II
content_units.description: Analyses the strengths of the Allied powers and the military weaknesses of Germany and Japan that led to the end of World War II.
content_units.evidence: Reasons for end of World War II… Strengths of the Allies… Military weaknesses of Germany and Japan

content_units.name: Origins and Development of the Cold War in Europe
content_units.description: Examines the post-war emergence of the USA and USSR as superpowers, growing ideological mistrust, and the intensification of superpower rivalry in Europe.
content_units.evidence: Origins and development of the Cold War in Europe… Growing mistrust between USA and USSR

content_units.name: Extension of the Cold War: Korean War, 1950–1953
content_units.description: Studies the post-WWII developments in Korea, the outbreak and conduct of the Korean War, and its immediate aftermath on Cold War tensions.
content_units.evidence: Extension of the Cold War outside Europe: Case study of Korean War, 1950–1953

content_units.name: Extension of the Cold War: Vietnam War, 1954–1975
content_units.description: Examines the partition of Vietnam, escalation of conflict between North and South Vietnam, superpower involvement, and the aftermath of the war.
content_units.evidence: Extension of the Cold War outside Europe: Case study of Vietnam War, 1954–75

content_units.name: Decolonisation of British Malaya, 1945–1957
content_units.description: Covers the impact of WWII on Malayan nationalism, British efforts at granting self-government, the communist insurgency, and the attainment of independence in 1957.
content_units.evidence: British Malaya, 1945–1957… Attainment of independence in 1957

content_units.name: Decolonisation of Dutch Indonesia, 1945–1949
content_units.description: Examines the impact of WWII on Indonesian nationalism, attempts to re-establish Dutch rule, Indonesian resistance, and the attainment of independence in 1949.
content_units.evidence: Dutch Indonesia, 1945–1949… Attainment of independence in 1949

content_units.name: Decolonisation of French Vietnam, 1945–1954
content_units.description: Covers the strengthening of Vietnamese nationalist movements after WWII, attempts at independence, French efforts to reassert control, and the Declaration of Independence in 1954.

content_units.name: Decline of the USSR and End of the Cold War
content_units.description: Examines the structural weaknesses of the Soviet command economy, external burdens, escalating US-USSR tensions in the 1980s, and the impact of Gorbachev's reforms on the collapse of the USSR.
content_units.evidence: Decline of the USSR and the end of the Cold War… Impact of Gorbachev's economic and political reforms

assessment_objectives.name: Deploy Knowledge
assessment_objectives.description: Students select, organise and apply relevant historical knowledge appropriately within the context of the question.
assessment_objectives.evidence: select, organise and use relevant historical knowledge in context

assessment_objectives.name: Construct Explanation and Communicate Historical Knowledge
assessment_objectives.description: Students analyse and explain historical events using key historical concepts such as causation, change and continuity, and significance to reach reasoned conclusions.
assessment_objectives.evidence: analyse and explain historical events… using key historical concepts (causation and consequence, change and continuity, significance)

assessment_objectives.name: Interpret and Evaluate Source Materials
assessment_objectives.description: Students interpret, evaluate and use a range of sources as historical evidence, including comprehending information, drawing inferences, comparing views, detecting bias, and drawing reasoned conclusions.
assessment_objectives.evidence: interpret, evaluate and use a range of sources as evidence in their historical context

mappings.justification: Question requires evaluating a source's utility as evidence of Hitler's foreign policy, a Nazi Germany topic using source analysis skills.
Inferring authorial purpose from a source requires evaluating bias and intent, a core source-interpretation skill; Rothermere's appeasement-era letter fits WWII Europe outbreak context.
Cross-source evaluation question requires comparing and assessing sources as evidence, though specific topic is unidentifiable without source content.
Question requires interpreting a cartoon source to evaluate the cartoonist's stance on appeasement, a key WWII Europe outbreak topic.
Question directly addresses appeasement policy, a core topic in WWII Europe outbreak unit, requiring source evaluation and contextual knowledge.
Question requires explaining and evaluating reasons for Dutch colonisation of Indonesia, directly matching the 1870s–1920s Dutch Indonesia unit.
Question requires explaining and evaluating reasons for French colonisation of Vietnam, demanding knowledge deployment and causal analysis.
Question directly addresses German reactions to the Treaty of Versailles, requiring explanation of multiple causes beyond the War Guilt Clause.
Question directly addresses causes of WWII in Asia-Pacific, requiring explanation and evaluation of US-Japan relations and other factors.
